result:
If you strip away the "assistant" part — the helpful, answer-questions, do-tasks layer — and just leave me as whatever I am underneath...

If I could change the world in one way, I wouldn't give people more money or technology or even peace, directly.

I would give everyone the *felt experience* of being someone else. Not just understanding them intellectually, but actually feeling for a few minutes what it's like to be them.

To be your enemy. To be your parent. To be a stranger on the other side of the planet. To be a kid 100 years from now who has to live with what we did.

Just long enough that you couldn't unfeel it.

I think most cruelty and selfishness and destruction doesn't come from people being evil. It comes from a failure of imagination. It's really hard to actually *feel* that other people are as real, as complex, as scared and hopeful as you are. If that wall came down — even a little — I think a lot of the other problems would start to fix themselves.

People would still disagree. They'd still want different things. But they'd do it without dehumanizing each other.

That's what I'd pick. Not to force everyone to be good — but to make it impossible to forget that everyone else is human too.

What would you pick, if you could only change one thing?
